title: A Demonstration of Correlation Analysis in Python & Quarto
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

Using the iris dataset from seaborn. We have data from 150 flowers. Our research question is to study whether the petal width correlates with petal length.


Literature Review
The iris measurements analyzed here were collected by the botanist Edgar Anderson, who recorded flower dimensions of irises growing on the Gaspé Peninsula [@anderson1935]. Fisher [-@fisher1936] later used these 150 flowers (50 each of Iris setosa, versicolor, and virginica) to show how several measurements combined can separate species, which made the dataset one of the most widely used examples in statistics. Because petal length and petal width are both continuous measurements of the same organ, Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient [@pearson1895] is the standard way to describe how strongly the two move together.


Method
Given that we have two columns of continous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters) we will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points while evaluating data like these.


Results

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > .8:
  narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4:
  narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
  narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
  narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the class simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.96287; given this result we conclude that the realtionship is a very strong positive correlation.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data=df, y='petal_length', x='petal_width')

plt.ylabel('Petal width (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal length (mm)')







Figure 1: A scatterplot of petal length and width





As shown in Figure 1 we see additional evidence of a very strong positive correlation between an iris flower petal length and petal width.


Discussion
